trialDescription: Use an isolated profile; do not change your daily profile first.
trialCommands:
# 1. Install into an isolated profile
dsh plugin --profile arbiter add /Volumes/sandisk/code/dsh-arbiter

# 2. Start that profile
dsh --profile arbiter web

# 3. Open the sidebar: Plugins → dsh-arbiter → configuration page
# 4. Pick a reviewer, create an allow / force-review rule, and run /arbiter status or the rule test
# 5. Check the logs page to see why each call was allowed or denied
executionExplanation: . The plugin does not modify host internals, does not switch your daily profile, and never answers sandbox escalation prompts on your behalf.
lifecycleDescription: After the plugin is disabled it adds no new verdicts; rules, candidates and audit records already written are retained. Uninstalling does not clean up SQLite automatically and does not switch existing sessions back to another preset; migrating a managed auto preset behaves like the official auto review, so confirm it in an isolated profile first.
calibrationLimit: Thresholds and the extra progress auto-approval scope are not calibrated; logs only give a lower bound on the failure rate, and the false-allow rate needs manual review.
surfaceLimit: Real human approval, surfaces other than Web, external-backend subtasks, MCP dynamic tool lists and background workflow composition were not validated in this round.
subagentLimit: Subtasks have no human channel; a call that would need one enters fallback-deny and only that call ends.
projectRulesLimit: Project rule files are treated as review guidance only by default; they are not human authorization and do not override plugin policy.
orderLimit: `prepend` does not guarantee that this plugin runs before other reviewers; internally the plugin guarantees that rules run before its own reviewer.
